issues.description: Method de.tum.cit.ase.Animal.messageOnFeed(): The problem statement's UML declares the abstract method as public ('+ messageOnFeed():String' in problem_statement.md), whereas the reference solution declares it as protected ('protected abstract String messageOnFeed();' in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java). This visibility mismatch can confuse students about the intended access level of the abstract method (whether it should be public to be called broadly or protected for restricted access) and may lead to divergent implementations or incorrect expectations about call sites.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent between specification and implementation. Preferred fix: change the reference solution to declare the abstract method as public (public abstract String messageOnFeed();) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java so it matches the UML and problem statement. Alternatively, update the UML and problem text to explicitly specify protected visibility and document the rationale (that package-level access or subclass-only access is intended). Ensure the chosen visibility is documented in the task description to avoid student confusion.
